top_story.headline: Drug Enforcement Administration buys its way into Detroit's Thanksgiving parade without competition
top_story.dek: The agency says only one organization can stage the parade, and the walk-in supports its Fentanyl Free America Initiative.
paragraphs: The Drug Enforcement Administration has posted a justification for skipping competition to take part in the 2026 America's Thanksgiving Parade in Detroit, Michigan, with Michigan's Thanksgiving Parade Foundation. The requirement comes from the agency's Detroit Field Division, and the period of performance starts 11/26/2026. According to the justification, participation 'will support the Fentanl Free America Initiative by increasing public awareness of the risks associated with illicity fentanyl' (typos as in the document), and 'DEA members will walk in the Parade with the American Flag and a DEA and Fentanyl Free America banner.'

The agency's stated reason is that the foundation 'was established with the sole purpose of staging and presenting the parade' and is the only organization able to do it. It cites the only-one-responsible-source authority (41 U.S.C. 3304(a)(1), FAR 6.103-1). The estimated amount line in the document is blank, so no value is given. USAspending shows no federal contract on record under the foundation's name. The justification was posted to SAM.gov as a Special Notice rather than in the Justification category.

sections.headline: Commerce Department adds $35.4 million to Accenture Federal Services' 20-year financial systems contract without competition
paragraphs: There are 36 new sole-source justifications today, 17 of them posted under other notice types. One is the Top Story, one is in the Washington, D.C. section and nine are in Extensions; none were left out as repeats. The 25 below range from a $35 million ceiling increase to routine parts and licenses. The Army justification for MANTech also carries an artificial intelligence tool name in its file properties.

blocks.text: Must read

blocks.title: Commerce Department adds $35.4 million to Accenture Federal Services' 20-year financial systems contract without competition
meta: only one company can do it
blocks.text: The Department of Commerce is modifying its Business Applications Solution contract with Accenture Federal Services LLC, competed in 2020 at $340,914,621.69 and now in option year six of 20. The justification says 'this modification would increase the total value of the Contract by $35,440,397.14', driven by user growth averaging over 80% and added licenses for Sunflower, PRISM and Oracle E-Business Suite, plus post-launch support for the National Institute of Standards and Technology rollout. It argues that because the contractor configured the system, no other contractor has the required knowledge or access.

blocks.title: Army plans to keep MANTech on commissary legacy computer systems worldwide without competition
meta: only one company can do it
blocks.text: On behalf of the Defense Commissary Agency, Army Contracting Command, Aberdeen Proving Ground intends a sole-source contract with one base year and four option years to run legacy applications across roughly 250 commissaries. It says the systems have over 4,000 custom-coded processes in COBOL and PL/SQL, and market research on 23 vendor capability statements found only the incumbent could avoid 'immediate and catastrophic failure'. The file's properties read 'Author: Gemini Enterprise; LastModifiedBy: Tokash, Nicole CIV USARMY ACC (USA)'; Gemini Enterprise is the name of an Google artificial intelligence product, and the metadata shows nothing more. It was posted as a Special Notice.

blocks.title: Veterans Affairs renews NetApp storage support for $4.5 million, saying replacement would cost $52 million

blocks.text: The Department of Veterans Affairs awarded ThunderCat Technology, LLC a brand-name NetApp hardware and software maintenance renewal on October 30 and posted the justification as an Award Notice. The justification says replacing the storage infrastructure would take about 12 months and cost approximately $52,000,000, 'considering the current shortages in storage devices due to Artificial Intelligence demand'.
Also worth a look

sections.headline: Labor Department keeps Education and Training Resources running the Wilmington Job Corps Center for $10.6 million without competition, citing two federal court orders
paragraphs: Nine new extensions or bridges today, mostly medical, lease and software continuity deals. Three stand out: a Job Corps center caught in litigation, a prison medical contract held up by a protest, and a second Army sewage bridge.

blocks.title: Labor Department keeps Education and Training Resources running the Wilmington Job Corps Center for $10.6 million without competition
meta: only one company can do it
blocks.text: The Department of Labor plans a one-year base contract of $7,548,685 (November 1, 2026 to October 31, 2027) plus a six-month extension of $3,057,697, with Education and Training Resources, the current operator. The justification says Job Corps administration 'is subject to two federal court orders' while the department assesses plans for a competitive contract, and that the incumbent contract expired October 31, 2026. It estimates sending students home would cost about $15,423 in transportation.

blocks.title: Bureau of Prisons extends NaphCare's medical contract at Brooklyn's federal jail for November while a protest is pending
meta: only one company can do it
Department of Justice, Bureau of Prisons
blocks.text: The Bureau of Prisons says it will buy comprehensive medical services for MDC Brooklyn from the incumbent NaphCare through monthly purchase orders from November 1 to 30, 2026, at an estimated $889,017.86 and prior Medicare benchmark rates. The justification says 'Award of a CMS contract is pending the resolution of a protest.'

It follows a four-month bridge awarded June 30, 2026, which was needed while the Army and the city negotiated 'a significant proposed rate increase' for a new ten-year contract. The justification says the city owns the only treatment plant connected to the base.

paragraphs: There are 246 new award notices and none were left out as repeats; 10 were flagged. The standouts are a $74.8 million program management award, a $3.5 billion health research ceiling and a $27 million furniture schedule award to a brand consulting firm.

It covers recruiting and monitoring Employment Networks, a contact center, a program website and payment administration. It is cost-plus-award-fee with a one-year base and four option years.

footer.known_gaps: No source errors were reported. OMB: no flagged apportionments or spend plans in the five-day window. USAspending is carried over from the morning edition. Of 2,003 attachments on 398 notices, 1,309 were queued for a later edition and 70 are access-restricted on SAM.gov; 28 files failed to read, and 8,255 files in all are queued for later editions.
